subject: Agriculture
title: Nitrogen-Fixing Bacteria
description: A micro-lesson that makes Nitrogen-Fixing Bacteria usable.

hook.text: Air is 78% nitrogen, but plants can't use it. It's locked in a form they can't absorb.

buildup.text: Rhizobium bacteria live in nodules on legume roots and convert atmospheric nitrogen into plant-usable ammonia.

discovery.text: This natural nitrogen fixation is why farmers rotate crops with legumes—clover, beans, and alfalfa enrich the soil.

twist.text: Adding synthetic nitrogen fertilizer suppresses these bacteria. Why fix nitrogen for free when it's already abundant?

climax.text: Organic farms rely heavily on biological fixation. It's slower but sustainable and costs nothing.

punchline.text: Bacteria do for free what factories do with fossil fuels.

quiz.question: How do Rhizobium bacteria help legume plants?
options: They convert atmospheric nitrogen into usable ammonia
They store water in root nodules
